guard_streams.source: Checklist for new phone or broadband contract
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-duration, pricing and cancellation protections are retail terms and do not establish network availability or parcel-measured performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom lists the contract checklist as last updated on 26 June 2026.
The checklist covers residential customers and small businesses with ten employees or fewer.
Contracts may be rolling monthly or fixed for 12, 18 or 24 months.
Providers must offer an option no longer than 12 months for each service.
Residential and small-business service contracts should not exceed 24 months.
A longer handset agreement must be separate from airtime, which cannot exceed 24 months.
Early-termination charges should not exceed the payments remaining on the contract.
The monthly price can be fixed or increase by a stated amount on a specified date.
The amount payable each month must be provided clearly before sign-up.
An increase beyond the agreed terms requires at least one month's notice and a penalty-free exit right.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom fines Virgin Media £28m for repeatedly preventing customers from cancelling contracts
guard_streams.write_limit: Enforcement findings about cancellation processes are consumer-protection evidence and cannot establish fixed-broadband coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the enforcement outcome on 8 July 2026.
Ofcom fined Virgin Media £28 million.
The findings concerned likely mishandling across nearly a three-year period.
The investigation found deliberate call dropping, unnecessary transfers and repeated holds.
Ofcom found the commission scheme effectively encouraged the cancellation-obstructing behaviour.
Ofcom's General Conditions prohibit cancellation procedures that act as a disincentive to leave.
Significant complaint volumes and unsuccessful prior engagement led Ofcom to launch the investigation.
The investigated calls ran from 1 January 2022 to 11 September 2024.
Ofcom concluded that Virgin Media's two-tier process and agent behaviour caused systemic and repeated cancellation failures.
The £28 million financial penalty is payable to HM Treasury.
